Registration could use a temporary email or device token, while the public profile exposes only a nickname. The posting system could accept text, images, and short video, with automatic deletion after a chosen period so that users feel less exposed. A queue would hide obvious slurs but leave borderline insults, insinuations, and coded language available because those forms generate engagement. To make the network difficult to shut down, the service could use multiple domains, a reverse proxy, cloud storage in more than one region, and a deployment process that recreates an instance when a host is removed.
